decisions.reason: As a newly launched safety shoe line in the firm’s core category, it is still an option with unresolved market potential and is likely worth keeping open for another year.

A comfort insole is relatively low-cost to keep on the market, so under real options logic the firm would likely continue it while learning demand, despite some risk of overlap with other insole offerings.
The supportive insole is also inexpensive to maintain but sits in a crowded insole set, so the firm would likely keep it for now while monitoring whether it proves distinct enough.
Its own dedicated page suggests strategic emphasis, and as an ergonomic safety shoe series tied closely to the firm’s innovation positioning it is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon.
Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialized niche, but the firm’s quality-focused protective-footwear capabilities make it sensible to keep this option open until demand becomes clearer.
Because it was presented as a flagship direction and featured on the home page, management would be very likely to retain it and continue learning from the market rather than abandon it early.
